newsitem.title: USA: U.S. soybean stocks plunge to 20-year low - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soybean stocks plunge to 20-year low - USDA.

text.p: Already tight stocks of U.S. soybeans, wheat and corn are expected to dwindle to even lower levels this summer and fall, the U.S. Department of Agriculture said on Friday.

Soybean stocks will slide to 125 million bushels, down 15 million bushels from the agency's estimate last month and the lowest level in 20 years, the department said in its monthly report of global supply and demand projections.

Commodity prices on the Chicago Board of Trade were expected to rise on the new government estimates. Market analysts had expected the Agriculture Department to trim the soybean stock figure only slightly, by five to 10 million bushels.

The latest soybean stocks estimate is the lowest amount of available inventory since the fall of 1973. Rising soybean prices and a forecast cut in soybean imports by Taiwan due to an outbreak of hoof and mouth disease were expected to reduce the pace of U.S. soybean exports, the Department said.

The monthly report also showed projected U.S. wheat stocks were down 14 million bushels from the previous month's estimate, to 460 million bushels. Stocks of corn were projected to be down 50 million bushels to 909 million bushels.
Analysts had expected the department to report declines for both corn and wheat stocks.
